# /crav1-tighten-spec

[All skills](../skills.md) · Walkthrough: [From a draft spec to an accepted spec](../../from-draft-spec.md) · Playbook: [`SKILL.md`](../../../.cursor/skills/crav1/crav1-tighten-spec/SKILL.md)

## Purpose

Walk an existing spec issue-by-issue.

One issue at a time, with explained resolutions (plus get a suggestion) and impact; patch only that issue after the user chooses. When the slice is partial or `## In the code` names paths, reads the committed code on the repo and branch the spec names before wording issues. A spec with no code behind it skips that read. Does not offer finish, add a test, or leave.

1.64.0: reads every listed work branch without checkout; a yes on writing the branch adds to the `Branch:` list; a listed branch that is gone and not merged is offered `(dropped)` (`mark-dropped`); a deleted branch whose work is in the base shows `merged, branch deleted`.

## Runs when

The spec is still mushy. Called by the user.

## Reads

In short: Spec, diagrams, ADRs, reviewer findings, and the committed code when the slice is partial or `## In the code` names paths.

Reads `spec.md`, diagrams, ADRs, reviewer findings already in the chat, and, when the slice is partial or `## In the code` names paths, the committed code on the repo and branch that spec names.

## Writes

In short: The picked issue in `spec.md`, the named diagram, ADR, or export when that pick says so, a branch line after a yes, and `Used by` on a quoted note.

Writes only the picked issue in `spec.md` and, when that pick says so, the named diagram, ADR, or export. Writes a branch onto the spec only after a yes. A stale research mark may be one issue. It does not clear the mark and it does not rewrite the research note.

## Does not

Leaves application code and unpicked issues alone. A spec with no code behind it skips that read.

Limits and exceptions: a different open repo or branch, a missing branch, a stub, or a spec too thin for that read stops and does not tighten. `suggest` does not patch. A disagreement with the code is called out and the spec is not rewritten to match the code. Finish, add a test, and leave are not choices here. A quoted note in `docs/notes/` gets its slug in `used_by` and a `Full source:` link; notes are never absorbed (1.61.0).
